In order to arrive at the said conclusion, the Tribunal has taken note of the medical evidence which indicated that the claimant had suffered 12% disability to the right upper limb and 18%
disability to the right lower limb and assessed the whole body disability at 10%.
3.
The evidence on record no doubt indicates that the claimant has suffered 12% disability to the right upper limb and 18% disability to the right lower limb.
However, it is also noticed that the claimant has suffered shortening of his leg by 1 inches.

In my view, having regard to the fact that there are disabilities to the right upper limb and right lower limb coupled with shortening of his leg by 1 inches, it would be appropriate to re-assess the disability at 20%.
4. As the accident is of the year 2012, the monthly notional income of Rs.7,000/- will have to be applied as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
5. Since the claimant has suffered 20% disability, 40% of the said income (Rs.2,800/-) would have to be added towards future prospects, which would result in the monthly income at Rs.9,800/-.

6. As the claimant was aged 18 years, as per the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121,
a multiplier of '18' would have to be applied.

sentences.text: 7. Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.4,23,360/- (Rs.9,800/- x 12 x '18' x 20%) towards loss of future earnings due to disability.
8. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards pain and suffering.
In my view, it would be appropriate to enhance the same to Rs.60,000/- under the said head.

9. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.22,000/- towards food, nourishment, conveyance,
attendant and other incidental charges.

In my view, having regard to the fact that the claimant was hospitalised for one month, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.30,000/- under the head of food, nourishment, conveyance, attendant and other incidental charges as against Rs.22,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
10. The sum of Rs.13,968/- awarded towards medical expenses by the Tribunal, being based on documentary evidence, does not call for modification and hence it is affirmed.
11. The Tribunal has not awarded any sum towards loss of income during laid up period.

Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimant, it would be appropriate to take the laid up period of the claimant as three months and award a sum of Rs.21,000/- loss of income during laid up period (Rs.7,000/- x 3 months).
